**Triage** — graded `p3`, `documentation`, `pm:queue`, routed `domain:spec`. Applied and read back first.

## Confirmed at `origin/main` `c616c2c`

```
packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.form.ts:24  { field: 'columns', …, helpText: 'Grid columns (default 12)' },
packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.form.ts:25  { field: 'gap',     …, helpText: 'Grid gap (Tailwind units)' },
```

Your distinction between the two lines holds and is the reason this card is precise rather than a style complaint: `12` is an author-visible fact about the grid they are laying out, so `columns` is fine; "Tailwind units" names a CSS library the app author never chose and cannot act on. ⛔ Leave `:24` alone.

## Why `p3` and why it is a real defect

The string is rendered verbatim in the customer-facing Studio property panel — the panel is spec-driven, feeding `dashboardForm` into the generic form renderer — so this is published product copy, not an internal note. An author reading it learns the name of an implementation dependency instead of what the number does.

`p3` because it is one string, nothing is broken, and the number still works whatever the label says.

## ⭐ The part worth preserving: you fixed the consumer and refused to fix the producer

objectui#7366 added a zh overlay saying something an author can decide (「组件之间的间距,数值越大越松」) and **deliberately left the English source alone**, because rewriting a producer's copy from the consumer is the second-dialect problem the contract rule exists to stop.

That restraint is what makes this card necessary and correct. The tempting move — one-line fix in objectui, ship it — would have left English and zh saying different things about the same field, with the divergence invisible from either side. Filing upstream instead is the expensive right answer, and it is the same producer/consumer discipline #14587 turns on from the other direction.

⚠️ Consequence for whoever takes it: once the English source says what the author decides, **the zh overlay in objectui#7366 becomes a translation of a different sentence.** Check it still reads as a translation rather than an unrelated improvement — and if the two have converged in meaning, the overlay may no longer be needed at all. ⛔ That check is in objectui, so it is a `repo:objectui` follow-up, not a file this card may touch.

## Scope

One `helpText` string. Say what the author decides — your "Space between widgets" is good — and let the numeric semantics live in the renderer.

⛔ Not Clause ②: `helpText` prose is not accept/reject behaviour and no public surface widens.

⛔ Do not sweep `dashboard.form.ts` for other framework-vocabulary leaks in this card. If there are more, they deserve a measured population the way #14628 did it — and note that `columns` already proves not every unit reference is a defect, so a blind grep for framework words would over-collect.

## ⭐ Premise check found a SECOND producer site for the same field, and this dispatch widens the card to it

Measured on `origin/main` `414c1fcf8` at 18:17Z, before claiming. The card and triage both name exactly one string. There are **two**, on the same key, and they feed **two different customer-facing surfaces**:

| # | producer | string on `main` | what it reaches |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.form.ts:25` | `helpText: 'Grid gap (Tailwind units)'` | the Studio property panel — **the card's site** |
| 2 | `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts:903` | `.describe('Grid gap in Tailwind spacing units')` (+ the JSDoc at `:902`) | `content/docs/references/ui/dashboard.mdx:36` — **not named by the card** |

Verified with a control that site 2 really is what the reference page publishes: the `columns` **helpText** (`Grid columns (default 12)`) appears **nowhere** in the `.mdx`, while `gap`'s **describe** appears verbatim as its table row. So the reference corpus renders `.describe()`, not `helpText` — two independent producer strings, two independent published surfaces.

**Seat ruling, open to the maintainer's or triage's veto: fix both, in this card.** The reasoning is the card's own. This card exists because objectui#7366 refused to fix a producer's copy from the consumer, since that would leave English and zh saying different things about one field. Fixing site 1 alone reproduces exactly that failure one level up: the Studio panel would say what an author decides while the published reference page still names a CSS library they never chose — the same divergence, relocated rather than removed, and invisible from either side.

⛔ **Triage's actual prohibition stands and is carried into the dispatch**: no sweep of `dashboard.form.ts` (or anything else) for other framework-vocabulary leaks. This is one field's two producer strings, not a population. ⛔ `columns` at `:24` and its `.describe()` sibling are untouched — `12` is an author-visible fact, as both the card and triage say.

## Also carried into the dispatch

- ⛔ Not Clause ②, no gate label, no contract-tier review.
- The `.describe()` edit regenerates `content/docs/references/ui/dashboard.mdx`. ⚠️ **Serial**: card #14477 is in flight and also regenerates under `content/docs/references/**`, but in `system/**`, not `ui/dashboard.mdx` — disjoint. If that changes, the later PR merges `main` through `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` and re-regenerates before enqueue.
- The objectui follow-up triage flagged is **owed and will be filed by the dev**: once the English source says what the author decides, the zh overlay from objectui#7366 becomes a translation of a different sentence, and may not be needed at all. That check lives in objectui ⇒ a `repo:objectui` card with a `Blocked-by` line, ⛔ not a file this card may touch.

## File-surface increment on the claim above — declared in-round, not at report time

My claim comment declared the two producer files. The landed diff is **five** paths. The three additions are all *derived artifacts of those two edits*, regenerated by the repo's own tooling and never by hand — no new judgement surface, and no sweep:

| path | why it is in the diff | produced by |
|---|---|---|
| `content/docs/references/ui/dashboard.mdx` | renders the edited `.describe()` | `check:generated --fix` (`gen:docs`) |
| `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.metadata-forms.generated.ts` | `en` is a mechanical copy of the edited form source | `check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write` |
| `.changeset/dashboard-gap-author-vocabulary.md` | the change ships from two published packages | hand-written, as required |

The i18n bundle is not a scope widening I chose. `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` names it for this change KIND, verbatim: *"edits a metadata form module ... a form edit drifts them from a package your diff never touches"*. Measured both ways on this branch: `pnpm check:i18n` exit **1** (`platform-objects: 1 bundle(s) drifted`) before the regeneration, exit **0** after. Leaving it out would have shipped a red gate.

⛔ Still no sweep: `columns` is untouched on both producer lines, and no other framework-vocabulary site was searched for or changed. The one leaf regeneration deliberately does NOT reach — the stale `zh-CN` translation — is filed as #15511, not ridden along.

## Deviations, declared rather than smoothed — posted separately so the report comment stays machine-clean

**1. I posted a claim comment even though the standing dev contract says the PM's claim already satisfies claim-first.** The dispatch required it, because `check-clause2-carriers.mjs` reads the GOVERNING claim — the newest one naming a branch — and mine would become that. Had I skipped it, the seat's `Clause-②: no` would still have governed; posting mine kept the predicate on the governing carrier either way. Verified by read-back: the line survives as `Clause-②: no` on its own line, and `readClause2Line` treats that spelling as `declared`. I did not touch `assignee`.

**2. The commit trailer carries a model identifier, which the same dispatch forbids elsewhere.** The hard rules say never put a model identifier in a commit message; the very next rule spells out the exact required trailer, which contains one. I read the prohibition as aimed at prose — title, body, code comments, changeset, doc and issue comments, all of which I kept clean — and followed the explicit trailer instruction, which is the more specific and more recent directive. No gate reads commit trailers (`check-agent-model-declared.mjs` governs `.claude/agents/**` frontmatter only, untouched here). Flagging it because it is a real conflict in the dispatch text, not something to resolve silently.

**3. Two gates are NOT MEASURED, and one narrowing is declared.** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3) and `check:i18n-coverage` (exit 3) both refused with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`; clearing the first needs a whole-repo `pnpm build`, which is CI's run and would have held the shared verify lock against other agents to measure something a prose-only diff cannot move. `check:react-declaration-parity` cannot run in this repo at all. Reported as unmeasured, never as passes. Everything else — including the repo-wide `pnpm lint` — was run whole rather than narrowed.

**4. The file surface grew from 2 paths to 5.** Declared in-round in comment 5545366885 rather than at report time, with the red-then-green measurement that forced the i18n one.

**5. Where the dispatch and the card disagree, as asked.** They do not, on anything material. The card and triage name one string; the dispatch widens to two. I re-ran the seat's control instead of inheriting it and it reproduces, so I acted on the widening. Triage's actual prohibition — no sweep, `columns` untouched — is stated identically in both and is held in both letter and spirit.

### Diff shape

**Five files**, derived three-dot (`origin/main...765da3a98`) — ⚠️ the two-dot form answers with 48 files here, because `main` has advanced far past the branch point and a two-dot diff shows main's own commits in reverse. | `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.form.ts` | 1/1 |
| `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts` | 2/2 |

Both producer sites now read `Space between widgets, in steps of 0.25rem (4 = 1rem)`. **`columns` untouched on both of its lines** (`helpText` and `.describe()`), the JSDoc moved with its describe, and the accept set is byte-identical: `gap: z.number().int().min(0).optional()` on `main` and at the head. `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 15512` → **✓ readable, both carriers agree.**

### The claim the whole wording rests on — verified at the pin, with one correction

The new text asserts a magnitude. If the renderer used a Tailwind class, "steps of 0.25rem" would be a new false sentence replacing the old one, so this was checked rather than accepted:

At the console pin **`00d3f09c`**, `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx` sets this key as an **inline style** inside `style={{…}}`:

```
gap: `${gap * 0.25}rem`
```

Linear, every accepted integer works, no scale gaps. The wording is correct against the actual consumer.

⚠️ **Citation correction.** The report cites `DashboardRenderer.tsx:1183`. At the pin the line is **1170**; **1183** is where it sits at objectui **`main`**. The bytes are identical at both revisions, so the conclusion is unaffected — but the citation points at a line number that does not exist in the tree this repo actually consumes. Recorded because "read the tree you actually ship against" is the discipline this lane keeps having to enforce.

⚠️ **And the "doubly wrong" claim needs narrowing, not repeating.** The report says "Tailwind units" named a dependency the consumer does not have. True **for this key** — but objectui does use Tailwind gap utilities elsewhere, including a sibling whose own doc comment reads *"Gap between items (Tailwind gap class, default: `gap-2`)"* (`components/src/renderers/action/action-bar.tsx:82`). So the old string was not wrong because Tailwind is absent from the platform; it was wrong because **this** key is inline-styled and never becomes a class. The narrower statement is the true one and the one worth carrying forward.

### Regenerated followers, and the level

`content/docs/references/ui/dashboard.mdx:36` and `en.metadata-forms.generated.ts:935` both carry the new string, and the `columns` row beside each is unchanged — the delta is one line in each, nothing outside. Changeset: `@objectstack/spec: patch` + `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`. Correct: published prose, no accept-set movement, no typed-surface change.

⭐ The `check:i18n` red the dev hit (`platform-objects: 1 bundle(s) drifted from the schema`) and cleared with `--write` is the right shape — the English bundle is a **derived** follower of the helpText, found by a gate the change kind selects, not by a sweep.

### ⚠️ What this PR knowingly ships as false, stated plainly

After this lands, `zh-CN.metadata-forms.generated.ts:935` still reads 「栅格间距(Tailwind 单位)」 while the English says something else. A zh Studio user keeps seeing the exact framework vocabulary this card exists to remove. The dev measured that regeneration **provably will not fix it** — merge fills gaps only, so `check:i18n` and `check:i18n-stale-fill` are both **green over the stale leaf**, and there is no digest for it either.

**The seat accepts filing over fixing (#15511), and not merely as the cautious option — it is the card's own principle applied one level over.** This card exists because objectui#7366 refused to rewrite a producer's copy from the consumer side. Writing new Chinese product copy from an English-language spec-lane dispatch is that same second-dialect error, just pointed the other way: it would put a wording judgement in the hands of the round least equipped to make it. What is *not* acceptable is letting it go unrecorded — hence #15511, and hence this paragraph rather than a silent ACCEPT.

### Cross-repo follow-ups, both verified present

It also answers triage's open question with a measurement rather than a guess: the English and the zh overlay have **converged on intent but not on content** (the new English carries the magnitude, the overlay carries only a direction), so "delete the overlay" is available but costs information. That is a better answer than the card asked for.
- **#15511** — open, for triage.

## What this card turned on

⭐ **The card named one producer; there were three.** The premise check before claiming found `dashboard.zod.ts:903`'s `.describe()` feeding the published reference page, and the dev then found `en.metadata-forms.generated.ts` — a generated English translations bundle — via `check:i18n` going red.
